newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS TUESDAY MIXED ON KEY UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS TUESDAY MIXED ON KEY UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted softer on the U.S. dollar and pound sterling but registered gains versus the mark and the rand in early Tuesday interbank trade, dealers said.

Dealers said the market was showing signs of returning to stability after the jitters caused by import pressure towards the close of last week, which saw players quoting wide bid/offer spreads to protect their positions.
"The market is pretty stable today and about U.S.$12 million long. Things should be back to normal by the end of this week," commented one dealer.
At around 0750 GMT the local unit was quoted at 11.7300/7400 on the U.S. dollar, marking a return to the normal one-point spread. It was however a touch weaker compared to late Monday's 11.7200/7400.

On the crosses, it also eased against sterling to 18.8760/9040 from 18.8700/9000 but was firmer on the mark at 6.3920/3950 compared to 6.4300/4500 and at 2.4985/5005 from 2.5050/5350 against the South African rand.
